meta.location: Jershon, Antionum, Manti, and the river Sidon
principles: Armor as an advantage that shortens a war

world_behind.title: Mormon sets the preaching aside deliberately
world_behind.text: Verses 1 and 2 say Alma and his sons kept preaching and that he will say no more about it. Twenty-one chapters of war follow.

world_behind.title: This begins the longest continuous block in the record
world_behind.text: Alma 43 through 63 covers roughly eighteen years of fighting. The scale is why recurring war vocabulary has to be treated once and then deferred.

world_behind.title: Zerahemnah staffed his command with dissenters
world_behind.text: Verse 6 says the Amalekites were more murderous than the Lamanites, so he appointed Amalekites and Zoramites as chief captains to keep the hatred up.

world_behind.title: Mormon gives both sides' aims side by side
world_behind.text: Verses 7 and 8 give Zerahemnah's designs: usurp power, bring the Nephites into bondage. Verses 9 and 10 give the Nephite design: lands, families, rights, and worship.

world_behind.title: The people of Ammon pay for the armies they will not join
world_behind.text: Verse 13 says they gave a large portion of their substance, and that the Nephites were compelled to fight alone. Alma 27 had set that arrangement up.

world_behind.title: Moroni is twenty-five
world_behind.text: Verse 17 gives his age at appointment. Mormon records it once and never returns to it.

world_behind.title: The armor decides the campaign before a battle
world_behind.text: Verses 19 through 22 have the Lamanites refuse to engage at Jershon because of breastplates and shields, and march around to Manti instead.

words.text: The Lamanite commander. The name occurs seventeen times, all in Alma 43 and 44, and never afterward. He is a Nephite dissenter leading an army against the country he left.

Shields worn on the arm. The compound occurs once in scripture. Mormon lists it between breastplates and head shields, and the whole equipment list is what stops the Lamanites from fighting at Jershon.
Treated at Mosiah 8:10, where Limhi's expedition brings back breastplates of brass and copper. Here they are Nephite issue, and the King James Bible uses the word only in Revelation, of locusts.

A plan made to deceive an enemy. The word occurs seven times in this record and never in the King James Bible, and six of the seven are in these war chapters. Mormon uses it here for the first time, of Moroni dividing his army to encircle the Lamanites.

Plate armor for the head. The compound occurs six times in this record and never in the King James Bible. Verses 38 and 44 use it twice, once of what protected the Nephites and once of what the Lamanites smote in two.

Fierce creatures, in the King James Bible usually inhabitants of ruins. The record uses the word three times and the King James Bible sixteen. Mormon uses it once as a simile for how the Lamanites fought under Zerahemnah's captains.

phrases.term: Alma, also, himself, could not rest
phrases.text: The last thing said of Alma before he leaves the record. Alma 45 gives his departure; here he is still going out to preach because he cannot sit still.
A whole people changes category in four words. Alma 35 ended with them stirring up the Lamanites; the war chapters open with the merger complete.

phrases.term: That they might worship God according to their desires
phrases.text: The last item in the Nephite list of aims, and the one Mormon expands in verse 10. He grounds the war in what the Lamanites would destroy rather than in what the Nephites would gain.

phrases.term: They had entered into a covenant and they would not break it
phrases.text: Mormon explains the people of Ammon in one clause. Their refusal is described as a promise held rather than as a policy, and it is why the Nephites fight alone.

phrases.term: He was only twenty and five years old when he was appointed chief captain
phrases.text: Moroni's age, given once. Mormon supplies it in the same verse that gives him all the command and the government of their wars.

phrases.term: They were naked, save it were a skin which was girded about their loins
phrases.text: The Lamanite army described by what it lacked. Mormon lists their weapons first and their clothing second, and verse 21 gives the effect: they were afraid despite outnumbering the Nephites.

phrases.term: Moroni, also, knowing of the prophecies of Alma, sent certain men unto him
phrases.text: A general consults a prophet about troop movements. Verse 24 has Alma report the Lamanite line of march, and the messengers carry it back.
Mormon's one simile for the Lamanite attack. It sits at the end of a verse listing what they broke: head-plates smitten in two, breastplates pierced, arms smitten off.

phrases.term: They were not fighting for monarchy nor power but they were fighting for their homes
phrases.text: Mormon states the Nephite cause by contrast with the enemy's. The list runs homes, liberties, wives, children, their all, rites of worship, and church.

phrases.term: Inasmuch as ye are not guilty of the first offense, neither the second, ye shall not suffer yourselves to be slain
phrases.text: The Lord quoted, giving the condition for defensive war. The permission depends on not having started it and not having escalated it.

phrases.term: Ye shall defend your families even unto bloodshed
phrases.text: The second half of the quotation, and the strongest thing in it. Mormon puts the whole justification of the Nephite war effort into two verses of quoted instruction.

verses.label: v. 1–3
verses.title: The handoff
verses.text: Alma and his sons go out preaching and Alma cannot rest. Mormon says he will say no more about it and returns to the wars, in the eighteenth year of the judges.

verses.label: v. 4–14
verses.title: Two designs
verses.text: The Zoramites become Lamanites and come under Zerahemnah, who staffs his command with dissenters to keep the hatred up. His aim is power and bondage. The Nephite aim is lands, families, rights, and worship. The people of Ammon keep their covenant and pay for the armies instead.

verses.label: v. 15–22
verses.title: Moroni and the armor
verses.text: Moroni takes command at twenty-five and meets the Lamanites at Jershon. His men have breastplates, arm-shields, head shields, and thick clothing; the Lamanites have weapons and a skin about the loins. They refuse the engagement and march for Manti.

verses.label: v. 23–30
verses.title: The intelligence
verses.text: Moroni sends spies and asks Alma to inquire of the Lord. Alma reports the line of march toward Manti and the intent to attack the weaker part. Moroni leaves guards, gathers the people of Manti, and hides his force by Sidon.

verses.label: v. 31–43
verses.title: The battle
verses.text: Lehi's division falls on the Lamanites at the crossing and drives them back over the river. Zerahemnah's men find Moroni waiting. The fighting is severe on both sides, and Mormon records what the armor stopped and what it did not.

verses.label: v. 44–47
verses.title: Why each side fought
verses.text: The Lamanites fight like dragons, inspired by their captains. The Nephites fight for homes and liberties rather than for monarchy, and Mormon quotes the Lord twice: not guilty of the first or second offense, and defend your families even unto bloodshed.

verses.label: v. 48–54
verses.title: The turn
verses.text: Moroni's men are about to break. He sends word that inspires them with thoughts of their lands and freedom; they turn, cry to the Lord in one voice, and the Lamanites flee to Sidon. Encircled on both banks and struck with terror, they are spared when Moroni orders the killing stopped.

chapter.title: Mormon states both war aims before any fighting
chapter.text: Seven verses of motive precede the first engagement. The reader is given what each side wanted before being shown what each side did.

chapter.title: The pacifists finance the army
chapter.text: The people of Ammon will not fight and give a large portion of their substance instead. Mormon records the arrangement plainly and calls the Nephites compelled to fight alone.

chapter.title: Armor changes the campaign without a battle
chapter.text: The Lamanites see the equipment and march twenty miles around. The first tactical event of the war block is a refusal to engage.

chapter.title: A general asks a prophet where the enemy is going
chapter.text: Moroni sends spies and a messenger to Alma in the same verse. Mormon shows revelation and reconnaissance used together and ranks neither.

chapter.title: Mormon quotes the Lord to justify the war
chapter.text: Two conditions: innocence of the first and second offense, and the duty to defend families. The justification is supplied as scripture rather than as Mormon's own argument.

chapter.title: The turning point is a thought, not a maneuver
chapter.text: Verse 48 has the men about to flee and Moroni inspiring their hearts with their lands and freedom. Verse 50 says the Lamanites broke in that selfsame hour.

chapter.title: The victory ends in an order to stop
chapter.text: Moroni sees the enemy's terror and halts the killing. The chapter that opens the war block closes on a commander declining to finish.

chapter.title: The war vocabulary is laid down here
chapter.text: Stratagem, arm-shields, head-plates, and breastplates all arrive in one chapter. Alma 43 is where these terms get their treatment for the twenty chapters that follow.

applications.title: Say what you are for before you say what you oppose
applications.text: Mormon listed the Nephite aims as lands, families, rights, and worship. When you are in a conflict, write down what you are actually protecting before you describe the other side.

applications.title: Pay for what you will not do yourself
applications.text: The people of Ammon funded the armies their covenant kept them out of. When your convictions exempt you from a burden others carry, find the contribution you can make.

applications.title: Ask and scout
applications.text: Moroni sent spies and a messenger to a prophet in the same breath. When facing a decision, use both the information you can gather and the guidance you can ask for.

applications.title: Remind people what they are defending
applications.text: Moroni's men were about to run until they were reminded. When someone is losing heart, name the specific thing at stake for them rather than urging them generally.

questions.text: What can I not rest from, and is it the right thing?
Who benefits from keeping me angry?
What covenant of mine would cost me if I kept it?
What am I giving to a cause I cannot join?
What was I trusted with young, and how did I handle it?
Am I fighting for something, or against someone?
When have I had the advantage and chosen to stop?
